prompt: A population of $2{,}000$ bacteria doubles every $5$ hours. Which function models the population $P$ after $t$ hours?
hint: Doubling fixes the base of the exponential. The harder part is the exponent, which must count doublings rather than hours.

hints.text: Doubling fixes the base of the exponential. The harder part is the exponent, which must count doublings rather than hours.
One doubling takes $5$ hours, so after $t$ hours there have been $\dfrac{t}{5}$ doublings. Use that as the exponent on the base $2$.
The model is $P = 2000(2)^{t/5}$, which is choice B.

learningObjective: Build an exponential model when the period differs from the time unit.
explanation: The population doubles, so the base of the exponential is $2$ and the starting amount is $2000$.
The exponent must count how many doublings have happened. In $t$ hours there are $\dfrac{t}{5}$ periods of five hours.
This gives $P = 2000(2)^{t/5}$. At $t = 5$ it gives $4000$, which is exactly one doubling, so the answer is choice B.

alternativeExplanations.title: Divide by the period, never multiply
steps: Choice A gives $2000 \cdot 2^{25}$ after 5 hours — astronomically wrong.
Whenever the growth period is longer than the time unit, the exponent divides.
The general form is $a \cdot b^{t/p}$, where $p$ is how long one full growth period takes. Test at $t = p$ to confirm you get exactly one growth step.
